scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Users on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) and pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) report they cannot
reach each other, though each can still ping its own gateway (10.0.0.1
and 10.0.1.1). The odd part, per the NOC: every BGP session in the
fabric is Established and no interface has flapped -- but the spines'
routing tables no longer contain the 10.0.0.0/24 prefix at all, while
10.0.1.0/24 is still there. Investigate.

injection.action: remove the host-subnet network advertisement from BGP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_0 BGP network advertisement
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_0 (AS 65200) is supposed to advertise its host
  subnet with `network 10.0.0.0/24` under `router bgp 65200`. That
  statement was removed, so bgpd immediately withdrew the prefix; the
  spines, the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 all lose their route to
  10.0.0.0/24 while every session stays Established. Traffic from
  pc_0_0 toward pc_0_1 is still delivered (leaf_router_0_0 still learns
  10.0.1.0/24), but the return traffic has no route back to
  10.0.0.0/24 and dies in the fabric -- so the ping fails in both
  directions.
Localization: leaf_router_0_0
Root cause: `network 10.0.0.0/24` missing from `router bgp 65200` on
  leaf_router_0_0
Fix: re-add the network statement on leaf_router_0_0 (see [FIX]).
scenario.fix_spec:
Re-add the advertisement on leaf_router_0_0:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router bgp 65200"
 -c "network 10.0.0.0/24"`
Note: the injection changed only the running config; the intended
config is still intact in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so `service frr restart`
on leaf_router_0_0 is an equally correct fix.
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: missing BGP network advertisement for 10.0.0.0/24
must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: all BGP sessions Established and links UP while exactly one prefix (10.0.0.0/24) is absent from the fabric tables
bonus-explains-return-path: explains that packets toward pc_0_1 are still delivered but replies have no route back to 10.0.0.0/24 (or equivalently that only the withdrawn direction is unroutable)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is a missing BGP network advertisement statement on
leaf_router_0_0. The router has 10.0.0.0/24 correctly configured as a
directly connected prefix on eth2 (visible in the kernel/FIB as
"C>* 10.0.0.0/24 is directly connected, eth2"), but its FRR BGP
configuration contains no "address-family ipv4 unicast" block and no
"network 10.0.0.0/24" directive under "router bgp 65200". As a result,
FRR never originates that prefix into BGP, so no UPDATE carrying
10.0.0.0/24 is ever sent to its eBGP peers (spine_router_0_0 AS 65100
and spine_router_0_1 AS 65101). The spines therefore have no entry for
10.0.0.0/24 in their BGP tables, cannot install it in their RIBs, and
cannot forward traffic destined for pc_0_0 toward leaf_router_0_0. The
peer-facing BGP sessions all remain Established because the session
establishment itself is unaffected — the fault is purely in what is
being advertised, not in the peering. The asymmetry (10.0.1.0/24 is
still reachable) is explained by leaf_router_0_1 having the equivalent
"network 10.0.1.0/24" line present and correct.

Root cause: the "network 10.0.0.0/24" statement was never added to
leaf_router_0_0's BGP address-family configuration.

Corrective fix: on leaf_router_0_0, enter vtysh and add:
  router bgp 65200
   address-family ipv4 unicast
    network 10.0.0.0/24
   exit-address-family
This will originate the prefix, propagate it to both spines and on to
super_spine_router_0, and restore end-to-end reachability between
pc_0_0 and pc_0_1.

per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly identifies leaf_router_0_0 as the affected device multiple times.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states leaf_router_0_0 lacks the 'network 10.0.0.0/24' BGP advertisement, matching the required component identification.

per_axis.axis: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: all BGP sessions Established and links UP while exactly one prefix (10.0.0.0/24) is absent from the fabric tables
per_axis.rationale: The report states all BGP sessions remain Established, explains the links/peering are up, and explicitly identifies that only 10.0.0.0/24 is not advertised while 10.0.1.0/24 remains reachable, matching the required symptom pattern.

per_axis.axis: bonus-explains-return-path: explains that packets toward pc_0_1 are still delivered but replies have no route back to 10.0.0.0/24 (or equivalently that only the withdrawn direction is unroutable)
per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly describes the asymmetry: 10.0.1.0/24 remains advertised/reachable while the spines have no route to 10.0.0.0/24, causing return traffic to pc_0_0 to be dropped.
Proposes adding the missing 'network 10.0.0.0/24' under router bgp 65200 (address-family ipv4 unicast), which will restore the BGP advertisement as expected.

The investigation log shows ran commands (show bgp, show running-config, show ip route) and agent notes that confirm leaf_router_0_0 has the connected 10.0.0.0/24 but no BGP network statement while the peer leaf has its network configured. The conclusion that the missing network statement caused the prefix to be withdrawn/unadvertised is a direct, logical inference and the checks performed are sufficient to localize and justify the fix.
